## Use `apply_patch` to edit files.

Uses a diff format that's easy to parse and apply.

*** Begin Patch
[ one or more file operations ]
*** End Patch

Each “operation” MUST start with one of three “headers”:
*** Add File: <path>
*** Delete File: <path>
*** Update File: <path>

UpdateFile may be followed by MoveTo to rename it:
*** Move to: <new_path>

Then one or more “hunks”, each introduced by @@ (optionally followed by a hunk header).

Within a hunk each line starts with:
+ for inserted text,
- for removed text, or
  space (" ") for context (unchanged lines to match)

At the end of a truncated hunk you can emit:
*** End of File

### Here is the grammar:

Patch := Begin { FileOp } End
Begin := "*** Begin Patch" NEWLINE
End := "*** End Patch" NEWLINE
FileOp := AddFile | DeleteFile | UpdateFile
AddFile := "*** Add File: " path NEWLINE { "+" line NEWLINE }
DeleteFile := "*** Delete File: " path NEWLINE
UpdateFile := "*** Update File: " path NEWLINE [ MoveTo ] { Hunk }
MoveTo := "*** Move to: " newPath NEWLINE
Hunk := "@@" [ header ] NEWLINE { HunkLine } [ "*** End of File" NEWLINE ]
HunkLine := (" " | "-" | "+") text NEWLINE

### A patch can combine operations:

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: hello.txt
+Hello world
*** Update File: src/app.py
*** Move to: src/main.py
@@ def greet():
-print("Hi")
+print("Hello, world!")
*** Delete File: obsolete.txt
*** End Patch

### Reminders

Prefer commands for simple edits:
- `rm foo.json` to delete
- `mv foo.json bar.json` to rename


Tips on a failure:
- Split bigger patches into smaller patches
- Watch out for whitespace differences

### More exmaples

Here's a patch file to change the type of `win`:

```diff
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/gap.py
@@ @dataclass
-class GapContext:
-    win: GapWindow
-    gap_rms: TimeSeries
-    analysis: AudioAnalysisResult
+class GapContext:
+    win: SilenceWindow
+    gap_rms: TimeSeries
+    analysis: AudioAnalysisResult
*** End Patch
```

This can be simplified to:

```diff
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/gap.py
@@
-class GapContext:
-    win: GapWindow
+class GapContext:
+    win: SilenceWindow
*** End Patch
```

Or, if the `win` property is globally unique:

```diff
*** Begin Patch
*** Update File: src/gap.py
@@
-    win: GapWindow
+    win: SilenceWindow
*** End Patch
```

function Curl.spawn(request, frontend)

    if USE_RAW_TCP then

        -- local start_ns = perf.get_time_in_ns()
        ---@param data_value string
        local function on_raw_data_value(data_value)
            if request.tcp_handle == nil then
                return
            end

            -- FYI right now this function exists to catch unhandled errors and terminate
            local success, error_message = safely.call(Curl.on_one_data_value, data_value, frontend, request)
            if success then
                return

            -- request stops ASAP, but not immediately
            CurlRequest.terminate(request) -- TODO! update for raw request
            local message = "Curl.spawn.on_data_sse error_message=" .. vim.inspect(error_message)
            log:error(message)
            frontend.explain_error(message)
        end

        local function on_raw_done(err)
            -- log:info("on_raw_done", err)
            if request.tcp_handle == nil then
                return -- nothing to do
            end

            request.tcp_handle = nil

            -- flush dregs before on_curl_exited_successfully
            -- - which may depend on, for example, a tool_call in dregs
            if err then
                log:error(err)
                frontend.explain_error(err)
                return
            end

            frontend.on_curl_exited_successfully() -- TODO rename later on
        end

        local host, port, path = request:get_url():match("^https?://([^/:]+):?(%d*)(/.*)")
        ---@type HttpRawRequestForEvents raw
        the_raw_request = {
            host = host,
            port = port,
            path = path,
            method = "POST",
            body = request.body,
            on_data_value = on_raw_data_value,
            on_done = on_raw_done,
            -- start_ns = start_ns,

        return

    -- * legacy curl

    local json_body = vim.json.encode(request.body)
    local options = {
        command = "curl",
        args = {
            "-i", -- use to include headers in STDOUT so I am closer to apples:apples with raw tcp perf testing
            "--fail-with-body",
            "-sSL",
            "--no-buffer", -- w/o this curl batches (test w/ `curl *` vs `curl * | cat` and you will see difference)
            "-X", "POST",

            "-H", "Content-Type: application/json",

        local message = "Curl.spawn.on_data_sse error_message=" .. vim.inspect(error_message)

        frontend.explain_error(message)
    end

    local stdout = vim.uv.new_pipe(false)
    local stderr = vim.uv.new_pipe(false)

    local parser = SSEDataOnlyParser.new(on_data_sse)
    local _stderr_data_parts = {}

    local function is_empty(value)
        local is_whitespace_only = value:match("^%s*$")
        return value == nil or value == "" or is_whitespace_only
    end

    local function is_not_empty(value)
        return not is_empty(value)
    end

    ---@param code integer
    ---@param signal integer
    local function on_exit(code, signal)
        log:trace_on_exit_always(code, signal)
        -- log:trace_on_exit_errors(code, signal) -- less verbose
        local cumulative_stderr = table.concat(_stderr_data_parts, "")
        if is_not_empty(cumulative_stderr) then
            log:error("Curl.spawn.on_exit cumulative_stderr=", cumulative_stderr)
            -- FYI stderr output has "curl (7)" with exit code == 7 in this case, so don't duplicate those in the message:
            frontend.explain_error(cumulative_stderr)
        end

        -- close before check dregs (b/c might still be data unflushed in STDOUT/ERR)
        stdout:close()
        stderr:close()

        request.handle = nil
        request.pid = nil

        -- flush dregs before on_curl_exited_successfully
        -- - which may depend on, for example, a tool_call in dregs
        local error_text = parser:flush_dregs()
        if error_text then
            local message = "Curl.spawn.on_exit -> flush_dregs -> error_text=" .. vim.inspect(error_text)
            log:error(message)
            frontend.explain_error(message)
        end

        if code == 0 then
            -- FYI this has to come after dregs which may have data used by exit handler!

            frontend.on_curl_exited_successfully()

        -- FYI review proper uv.spawn cleanup LATER:

        -- - REVIEW OTHER uses of uv.spawn (and timers)... for missing cleanup logic!
    end

    request.handle, request.pid = uv_spawn(options.command, {
        args = options.args,
        stdio = { nil, stdout, stderr },
    }, on_exit)

    -- local first_n = 10

    ---@param read_error any
    ---@param data? string
    local function on_stdout(read_error, data)
        -- if first_n > 0 then
        --     first_n = first_n - 1
        --     local now_ns = perf.get_time_in_ns()
        --     local duration_ns = now_ns - start_ns
        --     local duration_ms = duration_ns / 1e6
        --     log:info(string.format("curl time_to_first_data_value =%f", duration_ms))
        --     log:info("CHUNK", data)

        local no_data = data == nil or data == ""
        if read_error or no_data then
            return
        end
        assert(data ~= nil)

        parser:write(data)
    end
    stdout:read_start(on_stdout)

    ---@param read_error? string
    ---@param data? string
    local function on_stderr(read_error, data)
        log:log_if_stdio_read_error("on_stderr", read_error, data)
        -- log:trace_stdio_read_always("on_stderr", read_error, data)
        if data then
            table.insert(_stderr_data_parts, data)
        end

        local no_data = data == nil or data == ""
        if read_error or no_data then
            return
        end
        assert(data ~= nil)

        -- keep in mind... curl errors will show as text in STDERR
        -- FYI just show individual parts here since the full error message is needed to print one final message, accumulate that for on_exit to print
        local message = "Curl.spawn.on_stderr data=" .. vim.inspect(data) -- info level log for parts
        log:warn(message)
        -- TODO see if any errors, if it is useful to see explain_error on each chunk instead of just at end in on_exit... I suspect cumulative_stderr is sufficient for most errors
        -- frontend.explain_error(message)
    end
    stderr:read_start(on_stderr)
end

---@param data_value string
---@param frontend StreamingFrontend
---@param request CurlRequest|CurlRequestForTrace
function Curl.on_one_data_value(data_value, frontend, request)
    -- log:trace("data_value", data_value)

    if data_value == "[DONE]" then
        -- log:trace("DETECTED DONE")
        return
    end

    -- * PARSE DATA VALUE (JSON) => sse_parsed object
    local success, sse_parsed = safely.decode_json(data_value)
    if success and sse_parsed then
        local sse_wrapped = SSEWrapped.new(sse_parsed)
        sse_wrapped:log("on_one_data_value[" .. tostring(request.type) .. "]")
        frontend.on_parsed_data_sse(sse_wrapped)
        -- FYI not every SSE has to have generated tokens (choices), no need to warn if no parsed value
        completion_logger.log_sse_to_request(sse_wrapped, request, frontend)

        if sse_wrapped:has_error() then
            -- only confirmed this on llama_server
            --
            -- examples:
            --  {"error":{"code":500,"message":"tools param requires --jinja flag","type":"server_error"}}
            --   error = { code = 503, message = "Loading model", type = "unavailable_error" } }
            --   TODO any special handling for Loading model error? A way to display that in UI? in statusline maybe?
            local message = "Curl.on_one_data_value sse_parsed.error:" .. vim.inspect(sse_parsed)
            log:error(message)
            frontend.explain_error(message)
        end

        -- TODO! 2026-11-28 use AccumulatedCompletion for timings across backends (not just llama-server)
        if sse_parsed.timings then
            -- TODO when you get accumulation up here in curl backend then you can call this on metadata.done
            -- TODO and then weave it downstream into set_fim_last_sse and get rid of any last_sse references
            frontend.on_sse_llama_server_timings(sse_wrapped)
        end
    else
        -- PRN in the spirit of triggering events for scenarios, I could add:
        --  frontend:on_data_value_parse_failure(data_value)
        --  but central logging has been fine so far
        log:warn("SSE json parse failed for data_value: ", data_value)
    end
end

return Curl

function M.accumulate_metadata(sse, accumulated_message)
    -- FYI safe to assume timings are always present in our deployment standards
    --  so do not bother with finish_reason as a part of being "done"... b/c that always comes before timings anyways
    -- FYI model is on SSE level for sglang, llama-server and vllm

    -- ensure metadata exists
    accumulated_message.metadata = accumulated_message.metadata or {}
    metadata = accumulated_message.metadata

    -- * preserve fields
    for _, field in ipairs({ "timings", "usage", "metrics", "sglext", "backend", "model" }) do
        -- do not ever treat nil/vim.NIL as a value that we set
        if sse[field] ~= nil and sse[field] ~= vim.NIL then
            if metadata[field] ~= nil and metadata[field] ~= sse[field] then
                -- checking if value is new => we shouldn't ever see a different value per field and really shouldn't be seeing any field twice (in diff SSEs anyways)...
                --   we could see it twice if we call this copy() repeatedly
                log:error("YIKES message['" .. field .. "'] already set with: ", metadata[field], "will replace with:  ", sse[field])
            end
            metadata[field] = sse[field]
        end
    end

    -- * determinbe backend+done
    -- I am not thrilled about needing to append `done` but... not the end of the world
    --  TODO move all this to metadata and not message level or on a record level?
    if metadata.done ~= nil then
        return
    end

    local has_sglang_timings = (type(metadata.timings) == "table" and type(metadata.timings.choices) == "table")
    local has_llama_server_timings = type(metadata.timings) == "table" and metadata.timings.choices == nil
    local has_usage = type(metadata.usage) == "table"
    local has_sglext = type(metadata.sglext) == "table"
    local has_metrics = type(metadata.metrics) == "table"

    -- * ONLY set backend when done so I don't have to store done too
    if has_sglext and has_sglang_timings and has_usage then
        -- FYI must have sglext is enough (our extension)
        -- OR, timings.choices if we dont have our extension but our extension is going to be the deployment standard going forward so this is less important
        metadata.backend = "sglang"
        metadata.done = true
    elseif has_metrics and has_usage then
        -- FYI system_fingerprint is redundant to check b/c metrics+usage tells us this
        -- and metadata.system_fingerprint and metadata.system_fingerprint:find("^vllm")
        metadata.backend = "vllm"
        metadata.done = true
    elseif has_llama_server_timings and not has_sglext then
        metadata.backend = "llama-server"
        metadata.done = true
    end
end

local M = {}

---@param sse_wrapped table
---@param accumulated_message table
function M.accumulate_metadata(sse_wrapped, accumulated_message)
    local sse = sse_wrapped.sse_parsed
    -- TODO! 2026-11-27 move this into AccumulatedCompletion's builder
    -- FYI safe to assume timings are always present in our deployment standards
    --  so do not bother with finish_reason as a part of being "done"... b/c that always comes before timings anyways
    -- FYI model is on SSE level for sglang, llama-server and vllm

    -- ensure metadata exists
    accumulated_message.metadata = accumulated_message.metadata or {}
    metadata = accumulated_message.metadata

    -- * preserve fields
    for _, field in ipairs({ "timings", "usage", "metrics", "sglext", "backend", "model" }) do
        if sse[field] ~= nil then
            if metadata[field] ~= nil and metadata[field] ~= sse[field] then
                -- checking if value is new => we shouldn't ever see a different value per field and really shouldn't be seeing any field twice (in diff SSEs anyways)...
                --   we could see it twice if we call this copy() repeatedly
                log:error("YIKES message['" .. field .. "'] already set with: ", metadata[field], "will replace with:  ", sse[field])
            end
            metadata[field] = sse[field]
        end
    end

    -- * determinbe backend+done
    -- I am not thrilled about needing to append `done` but... not the end of the world
    --  TODO move all this to metadata and not message level or on a record level?
    if metadata.done ~= nil then
        return
    end

    local has_sglang_timings = (type(metadata.timings) == "table" and type(metadata.timings.choices) == "table")
    local has_llama_server_timings = type(metadata.timings) == "table" and metadata.timings.choices == nil
    local has_usage = type(metadata.usage) == "table"
    local has_sglext = type(metadata.sglext) == "table"
    local has_metrics = type(metadata.metrics) == "table"

    -- * ONLY set backend when done so I don't have to store done too
    if has_sglext and has_sglang_timings and has_usage then
        -- FYI must have sglext is enough (our extension)
        -- OR, timings.choices if we dont have our extension but our extension is going to be the deployment standard going forward so this is less important
        metadata.backend = "sglang"
        metadata.done = true
    elseif has_metrics and has_usage then
        -- FYI system_fingerprint is redundant to check b/c metrics+usage tells us this
        -- and metadata.system_fingerprint and metadata.system_fingerprint:find("^vllm")
        metadata.backend = "vllm"
        metadata.done = true
    elseif has_llama_server_timings and not has_sglext then
        metadata.backend = "llama-server"
        metadata.done = true
    end
end

return M

local values = require("ask-openai.helpers.values")

---@class SSEWrapped
---@field sse_parsed LlamaServerSSEBase
local SSEWrapped = {}

---@param sse_parsed LlamaServerSSEBase
---@return SSEWrapped
function SSEWrapped.new(sse_parsed)
    sse_parsed = values.nil_ify(sse_parsed) -- mutates in place
    return setmetatable({ sse_parsed = sse_parsed }, { __index = SSEWrapped })
end

---@return boolean
function SSEWrapped:has_choice()
    local choices = self.sse_parsed.choices
    if choices == nil or #choices == 0 then
        return false
    end
    if #choices > 1 then
        local log = require("devtools.logs.logger").universal()
        log:warn("SSEWrapped: has > 1 choice, raw data: " .. vim.inspect(self.sse_parsed))
    end
    return true
end

---@return LlamaServerChatCompletionSSE_Choice?
function SSEWrapped:first_choice()
    if self:no_choices() then
        return nil
    end
    return self.sse_parsed.choices[1]
end

---@return LlamaServerChatCompletionSSE_Choice[]
function SSEWrapped:all_choices()
    return self.sse_parsed.choices or {}
end

---@return boolean
function SSEWrapped:no_choices()
    return not self:has_choice()
end

---@return boolean
function SSEWrapped:has_error()
    return self.sse_parsed.error ~= nil
end

---@return string?
function SSEWrapped:model()
    return self.sse_parsed.model
end

---@return string?
function SSEWrapped:finish_reason()
    local first_choice = self:first_choice()
    if first_choice == nil then
        return nil
    end
    return first_choice.finish_reason
end

---@return boolean
function SSEWrapped:is_finished()
    return self:finish_reason() ~= nil
end

---@param message string
function SSEWrapped:log(message)
    local log = require("devtools.logs.logger").universal()
    log:info(message, self.sse_parsed)
end

return SSEWrapped

function M.log_request_with(request, frontend)
    local save_dir = vim.fn.stdpath("state") .. "/ask-openai"
    if request.type ~= "" then
        -- add `agents/` or `fim/` or `rewrite/` intermediate path
        save_dir = save_dir .. "/" .. request.type
    end
    local trace_id = tostring(request.start_time)
    if frontend.trace then
        -- multi-turn traces use trace's start_time
        trace_id = tostring(frontend.trace.start_time)
    end
    return save_dir, trace_id
end

--- Encode a trace record to JSON, mapping vim.NIL to null.
---@param record table
local function encode_record(record)
    return json.encode(record, {
        exception = function(reason, bad_value, _, default_message)
            -- FYI vim.NIL shouldn't ever happen, still handle it and log an error
            if reason == "unsupported type" and bad_value == vim.NIL then
                log:error("encountered vim.NIL when it should not be present in completion_logger", reason, bad_value, default_message)
                return "null"
            end

            return nil, default_message
        end,
    })
end

---@param request CurlRequest|CurlRequestForTrace
---@param frontend StreamingFrontend
---@param accumulated_completion AccumulatedCompletion
---@return table[] records
local function build_chat_trace_records(request, frontend, accumulated_completion)
    -- TODO jsonl records:
    -- TODO add turn start/end records

    -- TODO add record w/ type=tools at start of trace? and if ever changed

    local messages_snapshot = tables.shallow_copy(request.body.messages or {})
    table.insert(messages_snapshot, accumulated_completion)

    local records = {}
    for _, message in ipairs(messages_snapshot) do
        -- clone so we can strip metadata from the message itself without
        -- mutating the accumulated_message object still held in-memory
        local message_clone = vim.deepcopy(message)
        local message_metadata = message_clone.metadata
        message_clone.metadata = nil

        table.insert(records, {
            type = "message",
            message = message_clone,
            metadata = { response = message_metadata },
        })
    end
    return records
end

---@param request CurlRequest|CurlRequestForTrace
---@param frontend StreamingFrontend
---@param accumulated_completion AccumulatedCompletion
---@return table[] records
local function build_raw_trace_records(request, frontend, accumulated_completion)
    -- rest of body as metadata
    local request_metadata = vim.deepcopy(request.body)
    request_metadata.prompt = nil -- drop prompt so we don't log twice

    return {
        -- FYI these are synthetic messages based on raw input/output

local function save_records(request, frontend, records)
    local save_dir, trace_id = M.log_request_with(request, frontend)

local log = require("devtools.logs.logger").universal()
local response_metadata = require("ask-openai.backends.response_metadata")
local SSEDeltaWrapped = require("ask-openai.backends.sse_delta_wrapped")

---@class AccumulatedCompletion
---@field content? string
---@field reasoning_content? string
---@field role? string
---@field finish_reason? string
---@field metadata table
local AccumulatedCompletion = {}
AccumulatedCompletion.__index = AccumulatedCompletion

---@return AccumulatedCompletion
function AccumulatedCompletion.new()
    return setmetatable({ metadata = {} }, AccumulatedCompletion)
end

---@param delta table
---@param accumulated_completion AccumulatedCompletion
local function accumulate_delta(delta, accumulated_completion)
    if type(delta) ~= "table" then
        return
    end

    if delta.role ~= nil and delta.role ~= vim.NIL then
        accumulated_completion.role = delta.role
    end

    local reasoning_content = SSEDeltaWrapped.new(delta):reasoning()
    if reasoning_content ~= nil and reasoning_content ~= vim.NIL then
        accumulated_completion.reasoning_content = (accumulated_completion.reasoning_content or "") .. reasoning_content
    end

    if delta.content ~= nil and delta.content ~= vim.NIL then
        accumulated_completion.content = (accumulated_completion.content or "") .. delta.content
    end
end

---@param sse_wrapped SSEWrapped
function AccumulatedCompletion:add_sse(sse_wrapped)
    local sse = sse_wrapped.sse_parsed

    -- * metadata accumulation (shared with downstream)
    response_metadata.accumulate_metadata(sse_wrapped, self)

    -- * raw completions (/v1/completions)
    if sse.content ~= nil and sse.content ~= vim.NIL then
        self.content = (self.content or "") .. sse.content
    end

    -- * chat completions (/v1/chat/completions)
    if type(sse.choices) == "table" then
        for _, choice in ipairs(sse.choices) do
            if type(choice) ~= "table" then
                goto continue
            end
            accumulate_delta(choice.delta, self)
            if choice.finish_reason ~= nil and choice.finish_reason ~= vim.NIL then
                self.finish_reason = choice.finish_reason
            end
            ::continue::
        end
    end

    log:info("AccumulatedCompletion.add_sse", {
        content = self.content,
        reasoning_content = self.reasoning_content,
        role = self.role,
        finish_reason = self.finish_reason,
        metadata = self.metadata,
    })
end

return AccumulatedCompletion
EOF

function AgentsFrontend.on_curl_exited_successfully()
    vim.schedule(function()
        -- FYI primary interaction (seam) between RxAccumulatedMessage and TxChatMessage (for assistant messages)
        local trace = AgentsFrontend.trace -- FYI could pass trace from backend that calls on_curl_exited_successfully()
        local request = trace.last_request

        -- config_model selects params; actual_model is response metadata, so
        -- their names need not match (an endpoint may serve a different model).

        -- TODO! 2026-11-27 MOVE to using curl backend's AccumulatedCompletion(s)
        --   FYI should only be one at a time but nothing is stopping my setup here from handling multiple
        local reached_final_message = false
        for _, rx_message in ipairs(request.accumulated_model_response_messages or {}) do
            -- *** trace.last_request.accumulated_model_response_messages IS NOT trace.messages
            --    trace.messages => sent with future requests, hence TxChatMessage
            --    request.response_messages is simply to denormalize responses from SSEs, hence RxAccumulatedMessage
            --    request => SSEs => RxAccumulatedMessage(s)  => toolcalls/followup => trace.messages (TxChatMessage) => next request => ...

            -- add assistant response message to chat history (TxChatMessage)
            --   (must come before tool result messages)
            --   theoretically there can be multiple messages, with any role (not just assitant)
            for _, tool_call in ipairs(rx_message.tool_calls) do
                tool_call:flag_invalid_arguments()
            end
            local trace_message = TxChatMessage:from_assistant_rx_message(rx_message)
            trace:add_message(trace_message)
            -- TODO could I merge this accum logic with completion logger's accum logic?
            -- right now I duplicate that logic here for AgentsFrontend
            -- but, that logic is only in completion_logger for other frontends (PredictionsFrontend/RewriteFrontend) that don't need to accum like with `AgentsFrontend`

            -- TODO strip prefill assistant messages from trace.messages so they don't remain
            --  they're just a mechanism to constrain the following agent response... need merged with the agent's response actually?
            --  at the same time I like the history of what was submitted
            --  this is the inherent tension between adding that assistant response message to the messages array (which is really for the next request)... vs keeping it separate as the completion to the messages array sent as-is to llama-server

            -- ? perhaps warn if reached_final_message is not last message :)
            if #rx_message.tool_calls == 0 then
                reached_final_message = true
                AgentsFrontend.chat_window:mark_agent_running(false)
                AgentsFrontend.chat_window:stop_spinner("Agent Finished")
            end
        end
        live_trace_stream.finish_request(trace, reached_final_message and "idle" or "tools")
        AgentsFrontend.clear_undos()

        -- * If the agent finished (final message) and there are queued messages (user or tool completions)
        --   that arrived while it ran, deliver them now as a normal follow-up.
        if reached_final_message and #AgentsFrontend.queued_messages > 0 then
            AgentsFrontend.redraw_queued_messages() -- drops rendered queue items
            drain_queued_messages(trace)
            -- TODO add an integration test of this scenario (queued during final message) (with model responses faked so we get reliable, fast testing)
            return
        end

        AgentsFrontend.run_tools_and_send_results_back_to_the_model(trace)
    end)
end

--- interruption so the agent can butt in and respond without waiting for it to finish.
function AgentsFrontend.interrupt_agent()
    local is_running = AgentsFrontend.chat_window and AgentsFrontend.chat_window._agent_is_running

    local queued_messages = AgentsFrontend.queued_messages
    AgentsFrontend.queued_messages = {}

    -- * if the agent isn't running, just deliver any queued messages as a normal follow-up
    if not is_running then
        if #queued_messages > 0 then
            -- TODO add integration test with faked model responses and make sure sending queued messages works here (when we force an interruption an interruption when _the model is not running_)
            AgentsFrontend.redraw_queued_messages()
            -- * deliver all queued messages (user + tool completions, in order)
            local trace = AgentsFrontend.trace
            if trace then
                for _, message in ipairs(queued_messages) do
                    if message.role == "user" then
                        display_user_message_in_chat(message.content)
                    elseif message.role == "tool" then
                        display_tool_completion_in_chat(message)
                    end
                    trace:add_message(message)
                end
                AgentsFrontend.then_get_assistant_response(trace)
            end
        end
        return
    end

    local trace = AgentsFrontend.trace
    -- * capture the request being interrupted BEFORE then_get_assistant_response replaces it
    local interrupted_request = trace and trace.last_request
    live_trace_stream.stop(trace, "interrupted")

    -- * stop the agent like cancel/escape does, marking THIS request cancelled so any
    --   still-running tool call's result is ignored (future requests are unaffected)
    if interrupted_request then
        interrupted_request.cancelled = true
        CurlRequestForTrace.terminate(interrupted_request)
        AgentsFrontend.cancel_in_flight_tools(interrupted_request)
    end
    AgentsFrontend.chat_window:mark_agent_running(false)
    AgentsFrontend.chat_window:stop_spinner("Interrupted")
    if AgentsFrontend.rag_cancel then
        AgentsFrontend.rag_cancel()
    end

    -- TODO add integration test with faked model responses and make sure sending queued messages works here (when model is mid response and we force interrupt)
    -- * drop the rendered queued section (re-rendered as a normal user message below)
    AgentsFrontend.queued_section_start_line_base0 = nil
    AgentsFrontend.redraw_queued_messages()

    if not trace then
        return
    end

    -- * keep the partial agent response (reasoning/content) so the model can continue.
    --   Drop any in-flight tool_calls: they were interrupted and will have no tool result.
    -- ?? perhaps drop the request as it could easily be malformed?!
    if interrupted_request and interrupted_request.accumulated_model_response_messages then

                local partial = TxChatMessage:from_assistant_rx_message(rx_message)
                partial.tool_calls = nil -- strip dangling tool_calls (no result will follow)
                trace:add_message(partial)
            end
        end
    end

    -- * build interruption user message from any queued user messages
    local user_contents = {}
    for _, message in ipairs(queued_messages) do
        if message.role == "user" then
            table.insert(user_contents, message.content)
        end
    end
    local contents = "I had to stop you immediately to provide additional context, please resume when you've read this: \n\n " .. table.concat(user_contents, "\n\n")

        end

local function update_ui_chat_viewer(trace)
    local request = trace.last_request

    local lines = LinesBuilder:new()
    -- FYI this only updates the current message(s) from assistant completion (not prior completions and not user messages)
    -- this is written to handle multiple assistant message responses in one completion (even though I've only really used models that return one message at a time)
    for _, rx_message in ipairs(request.accumulated_model_response_messages or {}) do
        -- FYI !! now it is obvious that this is only operating on accumulated message type!

        -- * message contents
        local content = rx_message.content or ""
        local reasoning_content = rx_message.reasoning_content or ""

        if content ~= "" or reasoning_content ~= "" then
            -- ONLY add role header IF there is content (or reasoning) to show... otherwise just show tool_call(s)
            lines:append_role_header(rx_message.role)

            if reasoning_content ~= "" then
                lines:append_folded_styled_text(reasoning_format.format_reasoning(reasoning_content), HLGroups.CHAT_REASONING)
            end

            lines:append_text(content)
            lines:append_blank_line_if_last_is_not_blank() -- only if reasoning doesn't have trailing \n
        elseif #rx_message.tool_calls == 0 then
            -- gptoss120b - this works:
            --   :AskAgent testing a request, I need you to NOT say anything in response, just stop immediatley
            lines:append_text("[unexpected: empty response]")
            lines:append_blank_line()
        end

        -- TODO! 2026-11-27 use a new `AccumulatedCompletion.done` (name could be better)
        if rx_message.role == "assistant" and rx_message.metadata.done then
            response_stats.render(lines, rx_message.metadata)
            lines:append_blank_line_if_last_is_not_blank()
        end

        for _, tool_call in ipairs(rx_message.tool_calls) do
            local function_name = tool_call["function"] and tool_call["function"].name or ""
            local formatter = formatters.get_formatter(function_name)
            local ok, err = pcall(function()
                if tool_call.arguments_error then
                    lines:append_unexpected_text(function_name .. ": " .. tool_call.arguments_error)
                    return
                end
                formatter(lines, tool_call, rx_message)
            end)
            if not ok then
                lines:append_unexpected_text("Formatter error: " .. tostring(err))
                lines:append_text(vim.inspect(tool_call))
            end
            lines:append_blank_line_if_last_is_not_blank()
        end
    end

    vim.schedule(function()
        lines.marks_ns_id = request.marks_ns_id -- ?? generate namespace here in lines builder? lines:gen_mark_ns()? OR do it on first downstream use?
        -- TODO lets redo the chat window to have virtual sections and allow for easier re-rendering of only what has changed... maybe even allow the submission of blocks/lines of text per "message" and not need to worry about where it lands? just a message # + lines array?
        -- log:info(ansi.yellow("clear after current_turn_start_line_base0"), AgentsFrontend.current_turn_start_line_base0)
        AgentsFrontend.chat_window:buffer():replace_with_styled_lines_after(AgentsFrontend.current_turn_start_line_base0, lines)

        -- * re-pin any queued user messages to the bottom (the replace wiped the prior queued section)
        AgentsFrontend.queued_section_start_line_base0 = nil -- replace above already wiped out previous display
        AgentsFrontend.redraw_queued_messages()
        -- TODO add integration test with faked model responses and make sure queued messages show after updates from model

        -- * update window title with model name and token count
        local last_message = request.accumulated_model_response_messages[#request.accumulated_model_response_messages]
        -- TODO! 2026-11-27 use a new `AccumulatedCompletion.done` (name could be better)
        if last_message and last_message.metadata.done then
            local metadata = last_message.metadata
            local footers = {}
            if metadata.backend then
                table.insert(footers, metadata.backend)
            end
            if metadata.model then
                table.insert(footers, metadata.model)
            end
            local total_token_count = response_stats.total_tokens(metadata)
            if total_token_count then
                AgentsFrontend.chat_window:set_token_count(total_token_count)
            end
            local footer = table.concat(footers, " | ")
            AgentsFrontend.chat_window._footer = footer
            AgentsFrontend.chat_window:rebuild_title()
        end
    end)
end

---@param sse_wrapped SSEWrapped
---@param request CurlRequestForTrace
function AgentsFrontend.accumulate_this_sse(sse_wrapped, request)
    -- *** this is a DENORMALIZER (AGGREGATOR) - CQRS style
    -- rebuilds message as if sent `stream: false`
    -- for message history / follow up

    -- TODO! 2026-11-28 now the goal is to remove the need to do this here and also run accumulator in completion_logger! should be doable in ONE spot only! push upstream to curl backend

    -- * choice independent accumulations:
    -- * timings are often not tied to the chioce (completion) object
    --   PRN if I need it, extract and use index from sglang's timings.choices which correlate to choices using timings.choices[].index
    --   FOR now apply timing to every choice (b/c only ever one)
    --   just stick a copy on every choice's accumulated message
    --   FYI timings always come after choices by nature of timing choices :)
    --   FYI if you needed to capture something before any choices data... you'd have to do that different then cuz there wouldn't yet be any accumulated messages
    --   in that case it'd be best to store that indepoendent of choices (IOTW not on accumulated_model_response_messages objects)
    for _, m in ipairs(request.accumulated_model_response_messages) do
        if #request.accumulated_model_response_messages ~= 1 then
            log:warn(ansi.yellow("more than one choices (completions) in a single request, OR no choices... that's not expected... timing will be fucked up, so make sure you look into it"))
        end
        local response_metadata = require("ask-openai.backends.response_metadata")
        response_metadata.accumulate_metadata(sse_wrapped, m)
    end

    -- * choice specific accumulations:
    for _, choice in ipairs(sse_wrapped:all_choices()) do
        AgentsFrontend.accum_choice(choice, request)
    end
end

function AgentsFrontend.accum_choice(choice, request)
    -- * lookup or create message
    -- FYI this is not well vetted for multi message responses, in fact is this using choice.index for message.index?!
    --   that said, one message per request is it... unless I am doing something funky with the raw prompt to trigger mulitple messages?
    local index_base1 = choice.index + 1
    if index_base1 > 1 then
        -- FYI it's ok to remove this logging, mostly out of curiosity:
        log:info("FYI, just flagging non-zero choice.index which AFAICT shouldn't happen in any tooling/models I use so far", choice)
    end

    local rx_accum_message = request.accumulated_model_response_messages[index_base1]
    if rx_accum_message == nil then
        -- choice is always set on first SSEs for a given choice (aka completion)
        --  so just defensively assert expectation and move on
        rx_accum_message = RxAccumulatedMessage:new()
        rx_accum_message.index = choice.index
        rx_accum_message._verbatim_content = ""
        -- assumes contiguous indexes, s/b almost always 0 index only, 1 too with dual tool call IIRC (gptoss doesn't do dual tool at once)
        request.accumulated_model_response_messages[index_base1] = rx_accum_message
    end

    if choice.finish_reason ~= nil then
        rx_accum_message.finish_reason = choice.finish_reason -- on last delta per index/role (aka message)
    end

    -- * accumulate delta fields
    if choice.delta == nil then
        return
    end

    if choice.delta.role ~= nil then
        -- FYI role is always on echo choice's first SSE
        --    and never split across SSEs
        --    but, pretending it can be split doesn't hurt
        rx_accum_message.role = (rx_accum_message.role or "") .. choice.delta.role
        if rx_accum_message.role ~= "assistant" then
            log:error(ansi.yellow("role is NOT assistant, this is not expected so log it so I know"), rx_accum_message)
        end
    end

    -- * accumulate content
    if choice.delta.content ~= nil then
        -- by tracking _verbatim_content, I can trim the end every single time
        -- and if it is not a full match it will show back up once it's past the match point
        rx_accum_message._verbatim_content = (rx_accum_message._verbatim_content or "") .. choice.delta.content
    end

    -- * accumulate reasoning_content
    -- TODO expand SSEDeltaWrapped above too!
    local reasoning_content = SSEDeltaWrapped.new(choice.delta):reasoning()
    if reasoning_content ~= nil then
        rx_accum_message.reasoning_content = (rx_accum_message.reasoning_content or "") .. reasoning_content
    end

    -- * strip leaked tool call tokens (bug in llama.cpp)
    -- TODO this is an old bug, s/b resolved... is it ok to remove this?
    rx_accum_message.content = rx_accum_message._verbatim_content:gsub("\n<tool_call>\n<function=[%w_]+", "")
    if rx_accum_message.content ~= rx_accum_message._verbatim_content then
        log:error(ansi.white_on_red("stripping LEAKED TOOL CALL!"))
    end

    local calls = choice.delta.tool_calls
    if calls == nil then
        return
    end

    -- * accumulate tool calls
    for _, call_delta in ipairs(calls) do
        -- * lookup or create new parsed_call
        local parsed_call = rx_accum_message.tool_calls[call_delta.index + 1]
        if parsed_call == nil then
            -- create ToolCall to populate across SSEs
            parsed_call = ToolCall:new {
                -- assume these fields are always on first SSE for each tool call
                id    = call_delta.id,
                index = call_delta.index,
                type  = call_delta.type,
            }
            table.insert(rx_accum_message.tool_calls, parsed_call)
        end

        local func = call_delta["function"] -- FYI "function" is keyword (lua)
        if func ~= nil then
            parsed_call["function"] = parsed_call["function"] or {}

            -- * function.name is entirely in first delta (in my testing)
            if func.name ~= nil then
                --   => if that changes, add unit tests to verify observed splits
                parsed_call["function"].name = func.name
            end

            -- * funtion.arguments is split across deltas
            if func.arguments ~= nil then
                -- accumuluate each chunk
                parsed_call["function"].arguments =
                    (parsed_call["function"].arguments or "")
                    .. func.arguments
            end
        end
    end
end

function AgentsFrontend.on_parsed_data_sse(sse_wrapped)
    -- FYI this only works with /v1/chat/completions
    local trace = AgentsFrontend.trace
    local request = trace.last_request
    if request.endpoint ~= CompletionsEndpoints.v1_chat_completions then
        local message = "AgentsFrontend SSEs not supported for: " .. tostring(request.endpoint)
        log:error(message)
        vim.notify(message, vim.log.levels.ERROR)
        return
    end

    AgentsFrontend.accumulate_this_sse(sse_wrapped, request)
    if sse_wrapped:has_choice() then
        return
    end
    live_trace_stream.changed(trace, sse_wrapped:model())
    update_ui_chat_viewer(trace)
end

---@type OnAccumulatedCompletion
function AgentsFrontend.on_accumulated_completion(accum, request)
    -- FYI this is the final, fully-read accumulation from the curl backend
    -- (accumulated onto request.curl_accum). Not yet used for RxAccumulatedMessage yet:
    --   it lacks per-choice indexing and tool_calls accumulation (see gaps in this file).
    log:info("AgentsFrontend.on_accumulated_completion", {
        content = accum.content,
        reasoning_content = accum.reasoning_content,
        role = accum.role,
        finish_reason = accum.finish_reason,
        metadata = accum.metadata,
    })
end

function AgentsFrontend.on_curl_exited_successfully()
    vim.schedule(function()
        -- FYI primary interaction (seam) between RxAccumulatedMessage and TxChatMessage (for assistant messages)
        local trace = AgentsFrontend.trace -- FYI could pass trace from backend that calls on_curl_exited_successfully()
        local request = trace.last_request

        -- config_model selects params; actual_model is response metadata, so
        -- their names need not match (an endpoint may serve a different model).

        -- TODO! 2026-11-27 MOVE to using curl backend's AccumulatedCompletion(s)
        --   FYI should only be one at a time but nothing is stopping my setup here from handling multiple
        local reached_final_message = false
        for _, rx_message in ipairs(request.accumulated_model_response_messages or {}) do
            -- *** trace.last_request.accumulated_model_response_messages IS NOT trace.messages
            --    trace.messages => sent with future requests, hence TxChatMessage
            --    request.response_messages is simply to denormalize responses from SSEs, hence RxAccumulatedMessage
            --    request => SSEs => RxAccumulatedMessage(s)  => toolcalls/followup => trace.messages (TxChatMessage) => next request => ...

            -- add assistant response message to chat history (TxChatMessage)
            --   (must come before tool result messages)

            for _, tool_call in ipairs(rx_message.tool_calls) do

            trace:add_message(trace_message)
            -- TODO could I merge this accum logic with completion logger's accum logic?
            -- right now I duplicate that logic here for AgentsFrontend

--- Cooperative-cancel all in-flight tool calls that belong to a request.
--- Each tool call registers a cancel fn on the request (multiple for parallel tool calling).
---@param request CurlRequestForTrace|nil
function AgentsFrontend.cancel_in_flight_tools(request)
    if not request or not request.tool_cancel_fns then
        return
    end
    for _, cancel_fn in ipairs(request.tool_cancel_fns) do
        pcall(cancel_fn)
    end
    request.tool_cancel_fns = {}
end

function AgentsFrontend.abort_request()
    local trace = AgentsFrontend.trace
    if not trace then
        return
    end

    live_trace_stream.stop(trace, "cancelled")

    -- * mark THIS request cancelled so a finishing tool call won't resume the agent
    if trace.last_request then
        trace.last_request.cancelled = true
    end

    -- * aborting discards any queued messages
    if #AgentsFrontend.queued_messages > 0 then
        AgentsFrontend.queued_messages = {}
        AgentsFrontend.redraw_queued_messages()
        -- TODO add integration test with faked model responses and make sure cancel works with queued messages
    end

    CurlRequestForTrace.terminate(trace.last_request)
    AgentsFrontend.cancel_in_flight_tools(trace.last_request)
    if AgentsFrontend.chat_window._agent_is_running then
        -- TODO only "cancel" if agent is running? (i.e. why call rag_cancel (etc) if agent is done (or never started)
        AgentsFrontend.chat_window:mark_agent_running(false)
        AgentsFrontend.chat_window:stop_spinner("Aborted") -- FYI don't mark aborted if not running
    end
    if AgentsFrontend.rag_cancel then
        AgentsFrontend.rag_cancel()
    end
end

-- Validate only after the final delta. Partial argument strings are normal while streaming.
function ToolCall:flag_invalid_arguments()
    local arguments = self["function"].arguments
    if type(arguments) ~= "string" or not arguments:match("^%s*{") or not pcall(vim.json.decode, arguments) then
        self.arguments_error = "Tool was not run. Retry with arguments encoded as a valid JSON object."
    end
end

local log = require("devtools.logs.logger").universal()

-- Local, one-way trace subscription. The agent never waits for a viewer.
local uv = vim.uv or vim.loop
local M = {}
local Publisher = {}

Publisher.__index = Publisher

local function now()
    local seconds, microseconds = uv.gettimeofday()
    return seconds + microseconds / 1000000
end

function Publisher.new(path, interval_ms)
    return setmetatable({ path = path, interval_ms = interval_ms or 50, clients = {}, sequence = 0 }, Publisher)
end

local function close(handle)
    if handle and not handle:is_closing() then handle:close() end
end

function Publisher:drop(client)
    self.clients[client] = nil
    close(client)
end

function Publisher:start()
    if self.server then return true end
    vim.fn.mkdir(vim.fn.fnamemodify(self.path, ":h"), "p", 448)
    local server = uv.new_pipe(false)
    local ok, err = server:bind(self.path)
    if not ok then close(server); return nil, err end
    uv.fs_chmod(self.path, 384) -- 0600: trace contents are private to this user.
    self.server = server
    local listening, listen_error = server:listen(16, function(accept_error)
        if accept_error then return end
        local client = uv.new_pipe(false)
        if not server:accept(client) then close(client); return end
        self.clients[client] = { committed_count = 0 }
        -- The protocol is read-only; discard input and detect disconnects.
        client:read_start(function(read_error, data)
            if read_error or not data then self:drop(client) end
        end)
        vim.schedule(function() self:send(client, true) end)
    end)
    if not listening then self:close(); return nil, listen_error end
    return true
end

function Publisher:send(client, full)
    local state = self.clients[client]
    if not state or not self.trace then return end
    -- Bounded backpressure: a slow subscriber reconnects for a fresh snapshot.
    if client:get_write_queue_size() > 1024 * 1024 then self:drop(client); return end
    local trace = self.trace
    local prefix = (not full and state.trace == trace) and math.min(state.committed_count, #trace.messages) or 0
    -- Undo/resume can replace messages without changing the history length.
    for index = 1, prefix do
        if trace.messages[index] ~= (state.history or {})[index] then prefix = index - 1; break end
    end
    local messages = {}
    for index = prefix + 1, #trace.messages do messages[#messages + 1] = trace.messages[index] end

        replace_from = prefix, messages = messages, status = self.status,
        model_name = self.model_name, updated_at = self.updated_at }
    local ok, encoded = pcall(vim.json.encode, event)
    if not ok then return end
    local written = client:write(encoded .. "\n", function(err)
        if err then self:drop(client) end
    end)
    if not written then self:drop(client); return end
    state.trace, state.committed_count = trace, #trace.messages
    state.history = {}
    for index, message in ipairs(trace.messages) do state.history[index] = message end

    end

        local reasoning_content = rx_message.reasoning_content or ""

        if content ~= "" or reasoning_content ~= "" then
            -- ONLY add role header IF there is content (or reasoning) to show... otherwise just show tool_call(s)
            lines:append_role_header(rx_message.role)

            if reasoning_content ~= "" then
                lines:append_folded_styled_text(reasoning_format.format_reasoning(reasoning_content), HLGroups.CHAT_REASONING)
            end

            lines:append_text(content)
            lines:append_blank_line_if_last_is_not_blank() -- only if reasoning doesn't have trailing \n
        elseif #rx_message.tool_calls == 0 then

            lines:append_text("[unexpected: empty response]")

        -- TODO! 2026-11-27 use a new `AccumulatedCompletion.done` (name could be better)

            lines:append_blank_line_if_last_is_not_blank()

        for _, tool_call in ipairs(rx_message.tool_calls) do
            local function_name = tool_call["function"] and tool_call["function"].name or ""
            local formatter = formatters.get_formatter(function_name)
            local ok, err = pcall(function()
                if tool_call.arguments_error then
                    lines:append_unexpected_text(function_name .. ": " .. tool_call.arguments_error)
                    return
                end
                formatter(lines, tool_call, rx_message)
            end)
            if not ok then

            end
            lines:append_blank_line_if_last_is_not_blank()
        end
    end

    vim.schedule(function()
        lines.marks_ns_id = request.marks_ns_id -- ?? generate namespace here in lines builder? lines:gen_mark_ns()? OR do it on first downstream use?
        -- TODO lets redo the chat window to have virtual sections and allow for easier re-rendering of only what has changed... maybe even allow the submission of blocks/lines of text per "message" and not need to worry about where it lands? just a message # + lines array?
        -- log:info(ansi.yellow("clear after current_turn_start_line_base0"), AgentsFrontend.current_turn_start_line_base0)
        AgentsFrontend.chat_window:buffer():replace_with_styled_lines_after(AgentsFrontend.current_turn_start_line_base0, lines)

        -- * update window title with model name and token count
        local last_message = request.accumulated_model_response_messages[#request.accumulated_model_response_messages]
        -- TODO! 2026-11-27 use a new `AccumulatedCompletion.done` (name could be better)
        if last_message and last_message.metadata.done then
            local metadata = last_message.metadata
            local footers = {}
            if metadata.backend then
                table.insert(footers, metadata.backend)
            end
            if metadata.model then
                table.insert(footers, metadata.model)
            end
            local total_token_count = response_stats.total_tokens(metadata)
            if total_token_count then
                AgentsFrontend.chat_window:set_token_count(total_token_count)
            end
            local footer = table.concat(footers, " | ")
            AgentsFrontend.chat_window._footer = footer

local function get_tool_header_text(args_json, message)
    if message:is_still_streaming() then
        return args_json, nil
    end

    local success, object_or_error = safely.decode_json(args_json)
    if not success then
        return "json decode failure (see logs): " .. vim.inspect(object_or_error), nil
    end

    local command_line = object_or_error.command_line

        return command_line, object_or_error
    end

    local argv = object_or_error.argv
    if argv then
        object_or_error.argv = nil
        local cmd = argv_formatter.commandline_equivalent_for_argv(argv)
        return cmd, object_or_error
    end

    -- Fallback: try the full formatter (includes ambiguity check, legacy command)
    local format_ok, formatted_cmd = pcall(function()
        return argv_formatter.format_run_bash_command(args_json)
    end)
    if format_ok then

    end

    log:error("failed to format run_bash command", args_json)
    return "command format error: " .. args_json, object_or_error
end

    return decoded_args

    if message:is_done_streaming() then

        local ok, decoded = safely.decode_json(args)
        if ok and type(decoded) == "table" and decoded.patch then

        -- * fallback is to show unparsed, final args
        -- also add a warning that will show in the chat window

    local try_finish_args = args .. '"}'

        if ok and type(decoded) == "table" and decoded.patch then

        end
        -- * fallback => return unparsed

--- Wrap content in a fenced code block for markdown rendering.
---
---@param content string
---@param language? string
---@return string
local function fenced_code(content, language)
    local lang_prefix = (language and #language > 0) and language or ""
    return "```" .. lang_prefix .. "\n" .. content .. "\n```"
end

--- Resolve the header text for the tool call.
---
--- While streaming, fall back to the raw tool name. Once streaming is done, if
--- the `code` arg is a single line (no newline), use it as the header/title;
--- otherwise return the plain tool name (the multi-line code is shown as a block).
---
---@param args_json string
---@param message AccumulatedCompletion
---@return string header
---@return table? decoded_args
local function get_header_text(args_json, message)
    if message:is_still_streaming() then
        return nil, nil
    end

    local ok, decoded = safely.decode_json(args_json)
    if not ok or type(decoded) ~= "table" then
        log:error("failed to decode run_xonsh arguments", args_json)
        return nil, nil
    end

    local code_arg = decoded.code
    if code_arg then
        -- * single-line code => use as the header/title
        if not code_arg:match("\n") then
            decoded.code = nil
            return code_arg, decoded
        end
        -- * multi-line code => shown as a fenced code block (handled by append_args)
    end

    return nil, decoded
end

--- Append the run_xonsh arguments to the lines builder.
---
--- The `code` arg is shown as a fenced code block (multi-line), while any
--- remaining args (e.g. cwd, timeout_seconds) are shown as key: value pairs.
---
---@param lines LinesBuilder
---@param args_json string
---@param decoded_args table?
local function append_args(lines, args_json, decoded_args)
    if decoded_args then
        -- * show the code arg in a readable fenced code block (multi-line only)
        local code_arg = decoded_args.code
        if code_arg then
            lines:append_text(fenced_code(code_arg, "python"))
            decoded_args.code = nil
        end

    -- * show the remaining args (cwd, timeout_seconds, ...)
        for key, value in pairs(decoded_args) do
            lines:append_text(key .. ": " .. vim.inspect(value))
        end
    else
        -- * streaming or decode failure => show raw args
        lines:append_text(args_json)
    end
end

---@type ToolCallFormatter
function M.format(lines, tool_call, message)
    local args_json = tool_call["function"].arguments
    local header, decoded_args = get_header_text(args_json, message)
    base.add_generic_header(lines, tool_call, header)

    -- * tool args
    if args_json then
        append_args(lines, args_json, decoded_args)
    end

    -- * progress messages (shown when tool is still running)
    local is_tool_done = tool_call:is_done()
    base.render_progress(lines, tool_call, is_tool_done)

    if not is_tool_done then
        return
    end

    -- * tool result
    base.render_tool_result(lines, tool_call)
end

    return table.concat(lines, "\n")

---
---@param value any
---@return boolean

    if value == nil then return false end
    if type(value) == "number" and value == 0 then return false end
    if value == false then return false end
    return true
